paras: The Gwonseon-gu Office opened on July 1, 1988. The district is in the southwest of Suwon, and it borders Ansan-si and Hwaseong-si to the west and south. When Paldal-gu was created in 1993, some neighborhoods (dong) moved to it, and more moved to Paldal-gu in 2003. In 2006 a new district office building opened in Tap-dong. The district office says the name "Gwonseon" comes from a story about a scholar named Yi Go, who gave up his office, lived in Suwon, and urged people to live kindly.

To the northwest, Chilbosan (Mt. Chilbo) and Yeogisan (Mt. Yeogi) stand around the district like a folding screen and block the cold wind. Four streams flow through the city: Hwanggujicheon, Seohocheon, Suwoncheon and Wonchollicheon. The district office writes that the district lies downstream of them, so the worry about flooding in heavy rain is relatively large.

paras: The Paldal-gu Office opened on February 1, 1993. It is the district that was newly added to Suwon after Jangan-gu and Gwonseon-gu were created in 1988. The current office building was newly built and opened in Maehyang-dong in 2014.

In the district head's greeting, Paldal-gu is described as a cultural city where Suwon Hwaseong and a long history are alive. Among the cultural heritage that the district office introduces is the Stele of National Master Jingak at Changseongsa Temple (Changseongsa Jingak Guksa Daegak Wonjo Tapbi). It was set up in 1386, during the Goryeo period. It was originally at Changseongsa Temple on Gwanggyosan (Mt. Gwanggyo). After the temple disappeared, it was moved in 1965 to its present place in Maehyang-dong.

paras: Yeongtong-gu was created on November 24, 2003. It is in the east of Suwon. Gwonseon-gu is to the west, Jangan-gu is to the north. It also shares a border with Paldal-gu, the central part of the city, and Yongin-si is a neighbor too. There are two stories about the name Yeongtong. One says the village is shaped like a yeomtong (heart). The other says the treasure in a well on a peak of Cheongmyeongsan (Mt. Cheongmyeong) connects (tong) with the spirit (yeong, 靈).

Wonchollicheon, a stream left in its natural state, flows through the middle of the district, and Cheongmyeongsan rises on one side. There are high-tech companies such as Samsung Electronics and Gwanggyo Techno Valley. Because of this, the district office describes Yeongtong-gu as a center of the IT industry.

paras: The land where Seongnam-si stands is thought to be the old site of Hanam Wiryeseong, which King Onjo of Baekje made his capital in 18 BC. In 1895 it became part of Gwangju-gun (Gwangju County) in Hanseong-bu. It became Gwangju-bu in 1896, and Gwangju-gun again in 1906. In 1971 the Gyeonggi-do Seongnam Branch Office was set up to govern Daewang-myeon, Nangsaeng-myeon, Dolma-myeon and part of Jungbu-myeon of Gwangju-gun. On July 1, 1973 it was raised to Seongnam-si.

In 1968, a project to build a housing complex in Seongnam was approved. In May 1969, people who had been removed from their homes in Seoul began moving in together. In 1989 the Sujeong Branch Office and the Jungwon Branch Office became the Sujeong-gu Office and the Jungwon-gu Office. In 1991 the Bundang Branch Office became the Bundang-gu Office.

paras: On July 1, 1988, Seongnam-si set up the Sujeong Branch Office and the Jungwon Branch Office. On May 1 of the next year, 1989, the Sujeong Branch Office became the Sujeong-gu Office, and Sujeong-gu was created. On the same day the first branch offices were set up, the Dolma, Daewang and Nangsaeng branch offices were closed.

In March 1990, the Seongnam Public Health Center was divided into the Sujeong Public Health Center and the Jungwon Public Health Center. In November 2015, Bokjeong-dong was split into Bokjeong-dong and Wirye-dong, so Sujeong-gu got a new neighborhood, Wirye-dong. In September 1991, when Bundang-gu was created, the areas of the legal neighborhoods (beopjeong-dong) among Sujeong-gu, Jungwon-gu and Bundang-gu were set again.

paras: Jungwon-gu began in July 1988 as the Jungwon Branch Office. The Jungwon-gu Office opened on May 1, 1989, and Bundang-gu was split off on September 17, 1991.

The Jungwon-gu Office presents two main attractions: the traditional market Moran Minsok Oiljang (Moran Folk Five-Day Market) and Seongnam High-Tech Valley, a center of high-tech industry. The Moran Folk Five-Day Market opens every five days, on days with a 4 or a 9, and is known as the largest folk five-day market in the country. The city hall's tourism website gives the address of Namhansanseong (Namhansanseong Fortress) as Eunhaeng-dong, Jungwon-gu. Namhansanseong became a World Heritage Site in 2014.

paras: Bundang-gu opened on July 1, 1991, as the Bundang Branch Office. On September 17 of that year, the Bundang Branch Office became the Bundang-gu Office. At this time, the areas of the legal neighborhoods (beopjeong-dong) among Sujeong-gu, Jungwon-gu and Bundang-gu were set again.

Yuldong Park (Yuldong Gongwon) is a lake park in Yul-dong, Bundang-gu. It has beautiful views of the lake, the lawns and the low hills. It is said to be called Yuldong Park because there were many chestnut trees (yul) there from the Baekje period. Inside the park are the tomb stone of Han Gye-hui, an official of the Joseon period, and a monument to the March 1st Movement. In 2008 and 2009, Pangyo-dong was divided into Sampyeong-dong and Baekhyeon-dong.

paras: The name Uijeongbu is said to come from a story about Taejo (Yi Seong-gye), the first king of Joseon. When Taejo was returning from Hamheung to Hanyang, he stayed for a while in Jeonjwa Village in today's Howon-dong. Ministers came all the way there to discuss state affairs. So, they say, the name of the highest government office, Uijeongbu (State Council), became a place name. In documents, it appears in 1912 as 'Uijeongbu-ri', a village name in Yangju-gun (Yangju County).

In the Goguryeo period the area was Maeseong-hyeon, in the Goryeo period it belonged to Gyeonju, and in the Joseon period it belonged to Yangju. In 1938 it was called Yangju-myeon. In 1942 it became Uijeongbu-eup, and in 1963 it was raised to Uijeongbu-si. The city tree is the willow. It is said this is because the oldest place name in Uijeongbu is 'Nogyang', which was used for about 1,000 years, and 'yang' means willow.

paras: The name Anyang (安養) comes from Anyangsa Temple, which is said to have been built by Wang Geon, the founder of Goryeo. The story says that Wang Geon was passing Samseongsan (Mt. Samseong) and saw five-colored clouds at the top of the mountain. He sent someone to look. Under the clouds, the person met a monk named Neungjeongirang, and they agreed with each other and built the temple.

In 2010, an excavation confirmed the place where Anyangsa Temple used to stand. This site, Anyangsaji, became a Gyeonggi-do Monument in April 2023. Anyang became Anyang-myeon in 1941, Anyang-eup on August 15, 1949, and Anyang-si on July 1, 1973. On October 1, 1992, the Manan-gu Office and the Dongan-gu Office were set up, making Manan-gu and Dongan-gu two districts.

paras: Manan-gu first opened in 1989 as the Manan Branch Office. It became a district in 1992, when Anyang-si started the district system. The name Manan comes from Manangyo (Manan Bridge), built over Samseongcheon (Samseong Stream) in 1795, under King Jeongjo of Joseon, in the hope that the people would live in peace. In 1989, the Anyang-si Place Name Committee followed this example and chose Manan as the name of the district.

The district office is in Anyang-dong. In Seoksu-dong there is Manangyo (Manan Bridge), a Tangible Cultural Heritage of Gyeonggi-do. The name Anyang-dong comes from a story that Anyangsa Temple was built around the year 900. 'Anyang' is said to mean an ideal world where everything is smooth and there is no suffering.

paras: The Dongan Branch Office was set up in 1989. Dongan-gu began in 1992, when the branch office became a district. In 1973, when Anyang-eup became Anyang-si, this area was four neighborhoods (dong): Bisan-dong, Gwanyang-dong, Pyeongchon-dong and Hogye-dong. In 1996 the district office building was moved, and the district office is now in Bisan-dong.

Anyangcheon, Haguicheon and Galhyeoncheon flow through Dongan-gu. Green space is the largest kind of land, followed by residential areas where people live. There are sports facilities such as the Comprehensive Stadium, the Anyang Gymnasium and a sports park. There are also traditional markets such as Gwanyang Market and Hogye Market.

paras: The name Bucheon first appeared in 1914. At that time, the Japanese colonial government combined Bupyeong-gun (Bupyeong County) and nearby areas to make Bucheon-gun (Bucheon County). Of its 15 townships (myeon), Gyenam-myeon, Ojeong-myeon and Sorae-myeon correspond to the land of today's Bucheon-si. The oldest name for this area before that was Jubuto, from Goguryeo.

In 757, under King Gyeongdeok, Jubuto was changed to the Chinese-character name Jangje-gun. It seems to have changed to Suju in 940. The name changed to Annam Dohobu in 1150 and to Gyeyang Dohobu in 1215. In 1973, Bucheon-gun was abolished and Sosa-eup was raised to Bucheon-si. In the 1990s, the Jungdong district housing-land development project was carried out, and the city grew quickly.

paras: Wonmi-gu was created in February 1993, when Jung-gu was split into Wonmi-gu and Ojeong-gu. Its name comes from Wonmi-dong, where the district office is. Wonmi-dong took its name from Wonmisan (Mount Wonmi), one of the important mountains of Bucheon. The district office was closed in 2016 and opened again in January 2024.

The district is in the middle of Bucheon-si. To the east is Guro-gu in Seoul, to the south is Sosa-gu, and to the west is Bupyeong-gu in Incheon. In the 1990s, new towns were built in Jung-dong and Sang-dong, and many people moved in. Today it is the center of Bucheon for government, business, education and culture, and it has both old neighborhoods and new ones.

paras: Sosa-gu began as Nam-gu (South District), which was created in 1988 when Bucheon first got districts. It changed its name in February 1993. It was named Sosa-gu because it is where the old Sosa village began, and because it was developed after Bucheon became a city in 1973. The district office was closed in 2016 and opened again in January 2024.

Sosa-gu is in the south of Bucheon. It has mountains such as Seongjusan (Mount Seongju) and Halmisan (Mount Halmi), so the land is low in the north and high in the south. To the west is Incheon, and to the south is Siheung. Roads were built early along the Gyeongin National Road and the Gyeongin Line train, so traffic was good. The Seohae Line subway opened in two stages, in 2018 and 2023, which made it easier to get to other places.

paras: Ojeong-gu was first created in February 1993, when Jung-gu was split. The district system was abolished in 2016, and the district was created again on January 1, 2024. When Bucheon became a city in 1973, this area was Ojeong-myeon (Ojeong Township) in Gimpo-gun (Gimpo County). It joined Bucheon-si in 1975. There are several ideas about where the name Ojeong came from. One is that there were many paulownia trees (ojeong comes from the word for paulownia). Another is that five mountains run down in a line.

Ojeong-gu is in the north of Bucheon. In the west, it meets Incheon along Gulpocheon (Gulpo Stream). Half of the district is greenbelt land, and some places have height limits because Gimpo Airport is close. So there are more small row houses and multi-family homes than apartment buildings. The land near Gulpocheon became rice fields after the Hangang Irrigation Association was set up in 1925. Even now, it is the place in Bucheon that grows the most rice.

paras: Gwangmyeong is in the middle of western Gyeonggi Province. Seoul is to the east and north, Siheung and Bucheon are to the west, and Anyang is to the south. In ancient times, it belonged to Goguryeo's Ingbeolno-hyeon (Ingbeolno County). In 757, under King Gyeongdeok of Silla, it was given the name Gogyang-hyeon (Gogyang County). In 1795, under King Jeongjo of Joseon, it became part of Siheung-hyeon (Siheung County).

In 1914, it became Seo-myeon (Seo Township) of Siheung-gun (Siheung County). In 1970, the Gwangmyeong branch office of Seo-myeon was set up, and in 1979, Seo-myeon was raised to Soha-eup (Soha Town). On July 1, 1981, Soha-eup and the Gwangmyeong branch office were joined to become Gwangmyeong-si, and it was separated from Siheung-gun. In the center of the city are Gureumsan (Mount Gureum) and Dogonae Pass. Overall, it is a low plain about 30 to 290 m above sea level.

paras: Around the year 100, in the Samhan period, the Pyeongtaek area was called Yeondal-bugok. Under King Jangsu of Goguryeo, it was called Busan-hyeon (Busan County), and under King Gyeongdeok of Silla, it was called Jinwi-hyeon (Jinwi County). In 940, under King Taejo of Goryeo, Jinwi-hyeon was placed under Suju, and its name was changed to Pyeongtaek-hyeon (Pyeongtaek County). In 1938, Jinwi-gun (Jinwi County) was renamed Pyeongtaek-gun (Pyeongtaek County).

In 1981, Songtan-eup (Songtan Town) was raised to Songtan-si. In 1986, Pyeongtaek-eup (Pyeongtaek Town) in Pyeongtaek-gun was raised to Pyeongtaek-si. In 1995, Songtan-si, Pyeongtaek-si and Pyeongtaek-gun were ended and joined into one, making today's Pyeongtaek-si. The city flower is the pear blossom, which brings to mind the pear, a fine farm product of this area. The city tree is the pine, which is strong against the cold.

paras: Dongducheon is a city at the northern end of Gyeonggi Province. In Joseon, Idam, one of the 34 bangni (districts) of Yangju-mok (a large provincial district), became the root of Dongducheon. In 1963, Idam-myeon (Idam Township) was raised to a town (eup), and its name was changed to "Dongducheon." On July 1, 1981, the town was raised to a city. In 1983, Sangpae-ri in Eunhyeon-myeon, Yangju-gun (Yangju County) was added to the city.

In ancient times, during Goguryeo, it was called Naeulmae. In 757, under King Gyeongdeok of Silla, its name is said to have been changed to Sacheon. Most of the land is mountains. There is Wangbangsan (Mount Wangbang) in the east, Machasan (Mount Macha) in the west, and Oknyeobong (Oknyeo Peak) in the north. Soyosan (Mount Soyo), which rises on the western slope of Guksabong (Guksa Peak), is described as the pride of the city.

paras: Ansan was originally Janghanggu-hyeon (also called Gosayaholcha-hyeon) of Goguryeo. Under King Gyeongdeok of Silla, it became Janggu-gun (Janggu County). In 1308, under King Chungnyeol of Goryeo, it was raised again to Ansan-gun (Ansan County), because it was the town where King Munjong was born. In Joseon, it was also often called "Yeonseong." According to the Ansan-gun Eupji (a record of Ansan County), this came from Gang Hui-maeng planting lotus seeds, which he had brought from Ming China, at Gwangokji Pond, and the lotus then spread widely.

In 1976, the Banwol new industrial city was built, and the number of people grew every year. On January 1, 1986, it became a city and took back its old name, "Ansan," to become Ansan-si. In December 1994, all of Daebu-myeon (Daebu Township) in Ongjin-gun (Ongjin County) joined Ansan-si. In November 2002, Sangnok-gu and Danwon-gu were created.

paras: Sangnok-gu is a district of Ansan-si that opened on November 1, 2002. At that time, the Sangnok-gu Office and the Danwon-gu Office were both created in Ansan-si, and Sangnok-gu started with 11 dong (neighborhoods). In 2004, Il-dong was split into Il-dong and I-dong, making 12 dong.

Sangnok-gu has Suambong (Suam Peak), the mountain that stands for Ansan-si, and Ansan Eupseong (Ansan Town Fortress), which was the first form of the town called Ansan. It is also a place where Danwon Kim Hong-do, Seongho Yi Ik and Choe Yong-sin were active. In 1995, the Suam-dong, Jangsang-dong and Jangha-dong areas of Siheung-si joined Ansan-si, and Ansan-dong was newly created.

paras: Danwon-gu is a district of Ansan-si that opened on November 1, 2002. The district name comes from Danwon Kim Hong-do, one of Korea's best-known painters. Kim Hong-do learned painting from childhood from Gang Se-hwang, who lived and worked in Ansan. In 1991, Ansan-si came to be called the "City of Danwon."

Danwon-gu describes itself as a land of culture and art. Every October, the Danwon Art Festival and the Kim Hong-do Festival are held. At important events, citizens gather at Danwongak (Danwon Pavilion) to ring the bell. There are also nine walking trails, such as the "Friendly Forest Path" on Bonghwangsan (Mount Bonghwang).

paras: The name Goyang was made in 1413, under King Taejong of Joseon, by taking one letter from each of two town names, Gobong and Deogyang. In the Goguryeo period, Dareulseong-hyeon (Dareulseong County) and Gaebaek-hyeon (Gaebaek County) were set up here. In the Unified Silla period, the names were changed to Gobong and Uwang. In the reign of King Seongjong, it was raised from a hyeon (county) to a gun (larger county).

Stone tools found around Tanhyeon-dong and Donae-dong show that people have lived here for at least 50,000 years. In the area where the Ilsan new town was built, Gawaji rice seeds were found that were judged to be 5,000 years old. There are Bukhansanseong (Bukhansan Fortress) and Haengjuseong (Haengju Fortress), and the city describes Haengju Daecheop (the Battle of Haengju) as a victory during the Imjin War (the Japanese invasions, 1592-1598). Goyang became a city in February 1992, and in 2022 it became a special-case city (teukrye-si).

paras: Deogyang-gu was created on March 1, 1996, together with Ilsan-gu. Four years earlier, in 1992, Goyang-gun (Goyang County) had been raised to Goyang-si. The name "Goyang" was made in the 13th year of King Taejong of Joseon (1413) by joining "Go" from Gobong-hyeon (Gobong County) and "Yang" from Deogyang-hyeon (Deogyang County).

On July 1, 2018, Sindo-dong changed its name to Samsong-dong. On January 3, 2022, Heungdo-dong and Samsong-dong were split into Heungdo, Samsong 1 and Samsong 2 dong, and Haengsin 3-dong was split into Haengsin 3 and 4 dong. This made the 21 dong it has now. About 64% of the district's area is development-restricted land (greenbelt).

paras: Ilsandong-gu was created on May 16, 2005, when Ilsan-gu was split into Ilsandong-gu and Ilsanseo-gu. Ilsan-gu had been created on March 1, 1996, together with Deogyang-gu. Before that, in 1980, Jung-myeon (Jung Township) was raised to Ilsan-eup (Ilsan Town), and in 1989, the development of the Ilsan new town was announced.

Traces of very early people have been found on the land of Ilsandong-gu. In Munbong-dong, Sarihyeon-dong and Jiyeong-dong, objects from the Bronze Age were found. In Seongseok-dong, Seolmun-dong and Sarihyeon-dong, many relics such as stone axes were found. On January 3, 2022, Jungsan-dong was split into Jungsan 1 and 2 dong, so there are now 12 dong.

paras: Ilsanseo-gu was created on May 16, 2005, when Ilsan-gu was split into Ilsandong-gu and Ilsanseo-gu. Ilsan-gu was first created on March 1, 1996, as one of two districts, together with Deogyang-gu. The name Goyang was made in the 13th year of King Taejong of Joseon (1413) by joining "Go" from Gobong-hyeon (Gobong County) and "Yang" from Deogyang-hyeon (Deogyang County). The district office is now at 1600 Jungang-ro, and it opened this new building in March 2019.

On January 3, 2022, Tanhyeon-dong was split into Tanhyeon 1 and 2 dong, and Songsan-dong was split into Deogi-dong and Gajwa-dong. There are now 11 dong. Of these, the largest is Gajwa-dong, and the smallest is Ilsan 1-dong.

paras: Gwacheon is in the middle-west of Gyeonggi Province, and Seoul is right next to it in the north. In the Goguryeo period, it was called Yulmok-gun (Yulmok County), and in the time of King Gyeongdeok of Silla, it was called Yuljin-gun (Yuljin County). In 940, under King Taejo of Goryeo, its name was changed to Gwaju. It became Gwacheon-hyeon (Gwacheon County) in 1413, Gwacheon-gun (Gwacheon County) in 1895, and Gwacheon-si on January 1, 1986.

The city describes Gwanaksan (Mount Gwanak) and Cheonggyesan (Mount Cheonggye) as rising here. From 1982, government offices began to move in. The National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art opened in 1986, and the National Gwacheon Science Museum opened in 2008. Seoul Grand Park opened in 1984 and Seoul Land in 1988, and the Gwacheon Racecourse moved here in 1989.

paras: The name Guri came about in 1914, under Japanese rule, when administrative areas were greatly reorganized. People took one letter each from Guji-myeon (the 'Gu') and Mangu-ri (the 'ri') and called the area Guri-myeon. The name Guji first appears in 1530 in the book Sinjeung Dongguk Yeoji Seungnam (a geography book of Korea) as 'Guji-myeon of Yangju-mok'.

In 1963, five villages including Mangu-ri went into Seoul, so Guri-myeon shrank to about the size of the old Guji-myeon. It became a town (eup) in 1973. In 1980 it joined Namyangju-gun, and on January 1, 1986 it became Guri-si. The foot of Achasan Mountain is described as the place in South Korea where the most Goguryeo relics have been found. Donggureung (the Donggureung Royal Tombs), a group of nine Joseon royal tombs, became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2009.

paras: Namyangju was split off from Yangju on April 1, 1980 and newly created as Namyangju-gun. In 1986, Guri-eup was promoted to a city and separated, and Joan-myeon was newly created. In 1989, Migeum-eup was also promoted to a city and separated. On January 1, 1995, Migeum-si and Namyangju-gun were merged to become Namyangju-si.

The area of today's Jinjeop and Jingeon was called Goruino in the Goguryeo period. It was renamed Hwangyang in Unified Silla and Pungyang in Goryeo. At that time, it is said to have had a name of its own, different from Yangju. In 2001, Jingeon-myeon and Onam-myeon were promoted to towns (eup), and in October 2019, Toegyewon-myeon also became Toegyewon-eup.

paras: In the 600s, Osan was Maehol-gun of Goguryeo. In 757, under King Gyeongdeok of Silla, it was Suseong-gun. In 1310, in Goryeo, it was called Suwon-gun, and in 1941 it became Osan-myeon of Suwon-gun. In 1949 it became Osan-myeon of Hwaseong-gun, in 1960 it was promoted to Osan-eup, and in 1989 it became Osan-si with six dong.

Osan City chose the crow as its city bird. The 'O' in the name Osan is the same as the character for crow (烏), so the city found the bird in its place name. The city describes the crow as a sacred bird from long ago. The city flower is the plum blossom and the city tree is the ginkgo tree. There is said to be a record that plum trees were common in Osan in the past.

paras: The name Siheung came from the area of today's Siheung-dong in Geumcheon-gu, Seoul. In 1795, under King Jeongjo, Geumcheon-hyeon was renamed Siheung-hyeon, and the place name 'Siheung' was born. The southern part of today's Siheung-si first met the name 'Siheung' in 1914, when Ansan-gun was abolished and Gunja-myeon and Suam-myeon joined Siheung-gun.

In January 1989, Sorae-eup, Gunja-myeon and Suam-myeon of Siheung-gun were promoted and became Siheung-si. The southern land, which was Ansan-gun in Joseon, has a story about lotus seeds. In 1463, Gang Hui-maeng planted lotus seeds he had brought from China at Gwangokji Pond in Hajung-dong. After the lotus flowers spread widely, the area has had the nickname 'Yeonseong' since 1466.

paras: Gunpo City Hall says it is still not clear where the name Gunpo came from. Many stories are told. One says villagers gave food to hungry government soldiers during the Imjin War (the Japanese invasions, 1592-1598). Another says the name came from a stream called Gunpocheon. Another says Qing soldiers stayed here during the First Sino-Japanese War.

In Goguryeo times the area belonged to Yulmok-gun, in Unified Silla to Yuljin-gun, in Goryeo to Gwaju-gun, and in Joseon to Gwacheon-hyeon. In 1914 it became Nam-myeon of Siheung-gun, and on May 1, 1979 it became Gunpo-eup. On January 1, 1989, Gunpo-eup was promoted to Gunpo-si, and in December 1994, four villages (ri) of Banwol-myeon in Hwaseong-gun were added to Gunpo-si.

paras: In 1914, Uigok-myeon and Wangnyun-myeon of Gwangju-gun were joined to make Uiwang-myeon of Suwon-gun. In 1936 its name was changed to Irwang-myeon. In 1949 it belonged to Hwaseong-gun, and in 1963 it joined Siheung-gun and became Uiwang-myeon again. It was promoted to Uiwang-eup of Siheung-gun in 1980, an eastern branch office was set up in 1983, it became Uiwang-si in 1989, and in 1993 the city hall moved to a new place.

In 2007, by law, the Chinese characters of Uiwang-si were changed from 儀旺市 to 義王市. The Citizens' Charter of Uiwang says the citizens have received the clear spirit of Baegunsan Mountain and the high spirit of Cheonggyesan Mountain. So, following the name Uiwang, the citizens promise to walk a true and right path.

paras: Hanam is close to the east side of Seoul. The Han River flows from the east to the west of Hanam, and Namhansan Mountain (with its fortress) lies to the south. The city is described as having a good natural environment. In the early Three Kingdoms period, King Onjo of Baekje made the area near today's Chungung-dong his capital and called it 'Hanam Wiryeseong' (Wiryeseong Fortress). It stayed the capital of Baekje until the time of King Geunchogo.

In the time of King Taejo of Goryeo, Hanju was renamed Gwangju, and that is when the name 'Gwangju' began to be used. The Hanam area was part of Gwangju for a long time, and in 1980 Dongbu-myeon was promoted to Dongbu-eup. In 1989, Dongbu-eup of Gwangju-gun and parts of Seobu-myeon and Jungbu-myeon were joined to become Hanam-si, and in 1991 housing land development began in Sinjang-dong and Changu-dong.

paras: Yongin was originally two towns, Yonggu-hyeon and Cheoin-hyeon. In 1414, under King Taejong of Joseon, the two towns were joined and called Yongin-hyeon. The name was made by taking one character each: 'yong' (龍) from Yonggu and 'in' (仁) from Cheoin. Later, Yangji-gun was added, and it is said to have become today's Yongin-si.

The Yongin area has been Baekje land ever since Onjo became king at Hanam Wiryeseong (Wiryeseong Fortress). In 1895, Yongin-hyeon was renamed Yongin-gun, and in 1914 it took in Yangji-gun and part of Juksan-gun. In 1996, Yongin-gun was promoted to a city and Yongin-eup was divided into four dong. In 2005, three district offices were set up: Cheoin-gu, Giheung-gu and Suji-gu.

paras: Cheoin-gu was created on October 31, 2005 by joining the historical center of Yongin-si and its eastern area. Its name comes from Cheoin Bugok (a small special district) and Cheoin-hyeon of Goryeo, and it means 'a place where kind people live.' The name Yongin was also made in 1414 by joining 'Yong' from Yonggu-hyeon and 'In' from Cheoin-hyeon.

The district was named Cheoin-gu to carry on the spirit of the Battle of Cheoinseong (Cheoinseong Fortress), where Goryeo stopped a Mongol invasion. The name Cheoin is still used today, as in Cheoinseong Fortress, the Cheoin Culture Festival and the Cheoin Music Festival. The district also has tourist facilities such as Everland, as well as universities and research institutes.

paras: Giheung-gu was made in 2005 by joining Giheung-eup and Guseong-eup. The name Giheung was made in 1914, when Gigok-myeon and Guheung-myeon and others were joined: 'Gi' from Gigok and 'heung' from Guheung. Guseong comes from a place name in the Goguryeo period, and it is the oldest administrative place name in Yongin.

Giheung-gu is in the west of Yongin. Cheoin-gu is to the east, Suji-gu to the north, and Suwon-si to the west. Roads to the Gyeongbu Expressway and the Yeongdong Expressway, as well as National Routes 1 and 42, pass through it. Semiconductor companies and research institutes are gathered here. There are also places to rest and have fun, such as Giheung Lake Park and the Korean Folk Village (Minsokchon).

paras: Suji-gu began on October 31, 2005, when three districts were set up in Yongin-si and the Suji branch office was promoted to Suji-gu Office. Suji-myeon became Suji-eup in 1996, and in 2001 Suji-eup was promoted to the Suji branch office. The name Suji came from 1914, when Sujin-myeon and Jinae-myeon were joined and called Suji-myeon, taking 'Su' from Sujin and 'ji' from Jinae.

The Gyeongbu Expressway, the Yeongdong Expressway and National Route 43 pass through the district. Subway stations include Jukjeon Station on the Bundang Line, and Dongcheon, Suji-gu Office, Seongbok and Sanghyeon stations on the Shinbundang Line. In 2021, Jukjeon 1-dong was divided into Jukjeon 1-dong and Jukjeon 3-dong, and Sanghyeon 1-dong was divided into Sanghyeon 1-dong and Sanghyeon 3-dong.

paras: Paju lies where the Han River and the Imjin River meet and flow into the West Sea (Yellow Sea), so it has had many banks and embankments since long ago. That is why 'Paju (坡州)' can also be explained as 'a village on top of an embankment.' It got its present name in Joseon. In 1459, King Sejo raised Wonpyeong Dohobu (protectorate) to a 'mok' (a large provincial district) and changed its name to Paju, because the queen's family home was there, it is said.

In 475, under King Jangsu of Goguryeo, it was Surihol-hyeon, and in 1895 Paju-mok became Paju-gun. In 1972 it took in Jangdan-myeon, Gunnae-myeon, Jindong-myeon and Jinseo-myeon of Jangdan-gun, and in 1996 Paju-gun was promoted to Paju-si. Gorangpo and Munsanpo, river ports on the Imjin River, were well known as places where goods gathered, because they were close to Hanyang (the old name of Seoul).

paras: There are stories about the name Icheon. In one, Wang Geon, the founder of Goryeo, was going to fight Later Baekje when he met a big river at Bokhacheon Stream. A man named Seomok guided him across safely. After Wang Geon won the war, he gave the place a name by taking the first character 'I' (利) and the last character 'cheon' (川) from the phrase 'Iseopdaecheon.' In another story, Wang Geon stopped in Icheon on his way south to fight and had his fortune told, and the phrase 'Iseopdaecheon' came up, so he gave the name.

In the early Three Kingdoms period, Icheon was Baekje land. In the time of King Jangsu of Goguryeo, it belonged to Goguryeo and was called Namcheon-hyeon. In 1444, under King Sejong of Joseon, it was raised to a dohobu (protectorate), and in 1996 Icheon-gun became Icheon-si. Icheon is known as a city with many artists who make ceramics and many related facilities. In July 2010, it became the first city in Korea to be named a UNESCO Creative City in the field of Crafts and Folk Art.

paras: Anseong was a land that Goguryeo, Baekje and Silla fought to take from each other. When it became Goguryeo land in the 5th century, Anseong was called Naehyehol. In 1362, under King Gongmin, Anseong-hyeon was raised to Anseong-gun, and in 1413, under King Taejong, it moved from Chungcheong Province to Gyeonggi Province.

In 1914, the three counties of Anseong, Juksan and Yangseong were joined into one, Anseong-gun. On January 1, 1963, Gosam-myeon of Yongin-gun joined Anseong-gun. Anseong-eup became a town (eup) on July 1, 1937. At that time, the places in Gyeonggi Province that became an eup were Suwon, Anseong and Gaeseong. On April 1, 1998 it became Anseong-si, and on June 1, 2001, Gongdo-myeon became Gongdo-eup.

paras: The name Gimpo was first used in 757, during the reign of King Gyeongdeok of Silla, when Geompo-hyeon (Geompo County) was renamed Gimpo-hyeon. A well-known story says the name came from "Tugeumpo," a tale of two brothers who threw gold they had found into a river. The name is said to mean "the port where gold was thrown." The land first appears in history in 475, during the reign of King Jangsu of Goguryeo.

In 1632, during the reign of King Injo, Jangneung (a royal tomb) was built on Bukseongsan Mountain, and Gimpo-hyeon was raised to a gun (county). In 1914, Gimpo, Tongjin, and Yangcheon were joined to form Gimpo-gun. In 1963, Yangdong-myeon and Yangseo-myeon became part of Seoul. In 1979, Gimpo-myeon became an eup (town), and on April 1, 1998, Gimpo-gun was raised to Gimpo-si.

paras: The name Hwaseong (華城) was given in 1794 by King Jeongjo, while he was looking at the site for a fortress to protect Suwon-bu (Suwon Prefecture) and Hyeonnyungwon (a royal tomb). He made the name while thinking of an old story from Jangja (Zhuangzi). The name is explained as showing his wish to make this land a rich and lively place and to enjoy it together with the people. Hwaseong-gun was created in 1949. The gun office moved from Suwon-si to Osan-eup in 1970, and to its present place in Namyang-eup in 2000.

Before that, in the Goguryeo period, the area was divided into Dangseong and Maehol. In 1413, during the reign of King Taejong of Joseon, Namyang Dohobu (protectorate) and Suwon Dohobu (protectorate) were set up. In 2001, Hwaseong-gun was raised to Hwaseong-si, and on January 1, 2025, Hwaseong became a special-case city (teukrye-si). In February 2026, four new district offices were opened.

paras: Manse-gu is also a district that was created on February 1, 2026, when Hwaseong-si set up four district offices. The Manse-gu Office is on Hyangnam-ro in Hyangnam-eup, and there is also an on-site civil service office in Namyang-eup.

Manse-gu includes Ujeong-eup, Hyangnam-eup, Namyang-eup, Mado-myeon, Songsan-myeon, Seosin-myeon, Paltan-myeon, Jangan-myeon, Yanggam-myeon, and Saesol-dong. It has three eup (towns), six myeon (townships), and one dong (neighborhood), and it covers the most areas of the four districts.

Hyohaeng-gu includes Bongdam-eup, Maesong-myeon, Bibong-myeon, Jeongnam-myeon, and Gibae-dong. It is a district with one eup (town), three myeon (townships), and one dong (neighborhood).

Byeongjeom-gu includes Jinan-dong, Byeongjeom 1-dong, Byeongjeom 2-dong, Banwol-dong, and Hwasan-dong. It is a district made up of five dong (neighborhoods), with no eup (towns) or myeon (townships).

paras: Dongtan-gu is a district that was created on February 1, 2026, when Hwaseong-si set up four district offices. The Dongtan-gu Office is on Dongtan-yeok-ro.

Dongtan-gu includes nine dong, from Dongtan 1-dong to Dongtan 9-dong. According to the history of Hwaseong-si, Dongtan-dong was created by division in 2007, Dongtan 2-dong in 2008, and Dongtan 3-dong in 2009. In January 2018, Dongtan-myeon was abolished, and Dongtan 5-dong, Dongtan 6-dong, and Saesol-dong were created. In November of the same year, the Dongtan Branch Office (Dongtan Chuljangso) was opened, and in July 2023, Dongtan 9-dong was created.

paras: Gwangju-si in Gyeonggi-do is in the middle of Gyeonggi, to the southeast of Seoul. The present name "Gwangju (廣州)" was given in 940, during the reign of King Taejo of Goryeo. In 983, during the reign of King Seongjong, Gwangju-mok (a large provincial district) was set up, and in 1907 it became a gun (county). More than 4,000 stone tools used by prehistoric people have been found in Gonjiam-eup. On March 21, 2001, Gwangju-gun was raised to Gwangju-si.

Because of the influence of the Gwangju Mountains, there is little flat land. The land is shaped like a valley surrounded by mountains, so a lot of dry-field farming is done. The city is said to grow especially many vegetables, such as tomatoes, cucumbers, and lettuce. Namhansanseong (Namhansanseong Fortress) was built in 1626, and the city describes itself as the home of Namhansanseong and of royal ceramics.

paras: In the Goryeo period, Yangju was Yangju-mok (a large provincial district). In 1395, during the reign of King Taejo of Joseon, the name of the administrative area was set as Yangju-gun. In 1506, the government office was moved to what is now Yuyang-dong. In 1922, the gun office moved to Sidun-myeon (now Uijeongbu-si), and in 2000 it moved back to its present place.

Uijeongbu split off from Yangju in 1963, Namyangju-gun in 1980, and Dongducheon in 1981. On October 19, 2003, Yangju became Yangju-si, a city that mixes urban and rural areas. Yangju City Hall introduces its intangible cultural heritage, such as Yangju Byeolsandae Nori (a traditional mask dance drama), its historic sites, such as Hoeamsaji (Hoeamsa Temple Site) and Onneung (a royal tomb), and Dobongsan Mountain and Sapaesan Mountain in Bukhansan National Park.

paras: Pocheon was called Mahol-gun in the Goguryeo period, Gyeonseong-gun during the reign of King Jinheung of Silla, and Cheongseong-gun during the reign of King Gyeongdeok. In early Goryeo it was called Poju, and in 1413, during the reign of King Taejong of Joseon, it was Pocheon-hyeon (Pocheon County). The name "Pocheon (抱川)" is said to use the characters meaning "to hold" and "stream" because no water flows in from outside, and water only flows out.

In 1914, Yeongpyeong-gun was joined to Pocheon-gun. In 2003, Pocheon-gun was raised to a si (city), and Pocheon-eup was divided into Pocheon-dong and Seondan-dong. At the Sanjeong Lake tourist area in Yeongbuk-myeon, there is a lake surrounded like a folding screen by Myeongseongsan Mountain and Gwaneumsan Mountain. Pocheon Art Valley, which was brought back to life from an old abandoned quarry, has a natural lake called Cheonjuho and rocky cliffs.

paras: In the Yeoju area, Golnaegeun-hyeon (Golnaegeun County) was set up in 475, during the reign of King Jangsu of Goguryeo, and in 940, during the reign of King Taejo of Goryeo, its name was changed to Hwangnyeo-hyeon. In 1305, during the reign of King Chungnyeol of Goryeo, it was renamed Yeoheung and raised from a hyeon (county) to a gun (county). In 1469, during the reign of King Yejong of Joseon, Yeongneung (the tomb of King Sejong the Great) was moved to the foot of Bukseongsan Mountain, and the area was raised to Yeoju-mok (a large provincial district). At that time, Cheonnyeong-hyeon was abolished and joined to Yeoju-mok.

Objects from the Paleolithic period have been found in the Yeoju area, and the Heunam-ri Prehistoric Settlement Site is well known as a Bronze Age site. In 1941, Yeoju-myeon became Yeoju-eup, and in 2013, Yeoju-gun became Yeoju-si. On December 31, 2021, the name of Neungseo-myeon was changed to Sejongdaewang-myeon.

paras: Along the Hantangang River in Yeoncheon, Homo erectus, said to be the first humans on the Korean Peninsula, are said to have begun living there about 300,000 years ago, in the Paleolithic period. The hand axes they left behind were found in 1978 at Jeongok-ri in Yeoncheon, the first such find in East Asia. In 675, Silla defeated the Tang army at Maecho-seong (Maecho Fortress) on the Hantangang River, and after that Yeoncheon became fully Silla land.

In 1309, in the first year of King Chungseon of Goryeo, the name of the gun was changed from Jangju to Yeoncheon, and in 1413, during the reign of King Taejong of Joseon, a Yeoncheon hyeongam (county magistrate) was placed there. In 1954, under the Act on Temporary Administrative Measures for Recovered Areas, it regained administrative authority from November 17 of that year. In May 1979, Yeoncheon-myeon became Yeoncheon-eup, and in October 1985, Jeongok-myeon became Jeongok-eup.

paras: Gapyeong is in a mountainous area in the northeast of Gyeonggi-do. In the Goguryeo period it was called Geunpyeong-gun or Simcheon-hyeon, and in 757, during the reign of King Gyeongdeok of Unified Silla, its name was changed to "Gapyeong." In 1413 it moved from Gangwon-do to Gyeonggi-do, and in 1507, during the reign of King Jungjong, it was raised from a hyeon (county) to a gun (county).

The Hongcheongang River meets the Bukhangang River and flows to the southwest, and Hwaaksan Mountain in the north is described as the highest peak of the Baekdudaegan (the main mountain range of Korea). In 1895 it was briefly part of Pocheon-gun in Gyeonggi-do, and one year later it became independent again as Gapyeong-gun. In 1973, Gapyeong-myeon was raised to an eup (town). In 2004, Oeseo-myeon was renamed Cheongpyeong-myeon, and in 2015, Ha-myeon was renamed Jojong-myeon.

paras: The name Yangpyeong (楊平) came about in September 1908, when Yanggeun-gun (楊根郡) and Jipyeong-gun (砥平郡) were joined and called Yangpyeong-gun. Yanggeun-gun was called Hangyang-gun in the Goguryeo period, and Jipyeong-gun was called Jihyeon-hyeon in the Goguryeo period.

In March 1914, Namjong-myeon went to Gwangju-gun, and in April 1942, Seorak-myeon went to Gapyeong-gun. In January 1963, Gaegun-myeon of Yeoju-gun joined Yangpyeong-gun. In May 1979, Yangpyeong-myeon became Yangpyeong-eup, and in December 2006, Jije-myeon changed its name to Jipyeong-myeon. The county explains that its symbol mark is based on the thousand-year-old ginkgo tree of Yongmunsan Mountain, and shows Yongmunsan Mountain and the meeting of the Namhangang River and the Bukhangang River.

paras: In the Samhan period, Cheongju was part of Mahan. In Baekje times it was called Sangdang-hyeon (Sangdang County). After Silla unified the Three Kingdoms, it was raised to Seowongyeong, one of the five secondary capitals, and became a center of local government. In the 23rd year of King Taejo of Goryeo (940), its name was changed to "Cheongju."

In the 3rd year of King U of Goryeo (1377), Jikji (the world's oldest surviving book printed with movable metal type) was printed at Heungdeoksa Temple in Cheongju. In the Joseon period, Chungju became a transport center because of its waterways, so Cheongju grew slowly. But when the Gyeongbu Line railway was built in 1905, it got a chance to grow. Cheongju-bu and Cheongwon-gun were split in 1946, and Cheongju became a city (si) in 1949. On July 1, 2014, Cheongju and Cheongwon were joined, and the unified Cheongju-si began.

paras: Sangdang-gu began as the Eastern Branch Office in July 1989. In January 1995, the branch office was raised to a district (gu), and the Sangdang-gu Office opened. When Cheongju-si and Cheongwon-gun were joined into one on July 1, 2014, the Sangdang-gu Office opened again. Today the district has 5 myeon (rural towns) and 8 dong (neighborhoods).

The district office describes Sangdang-gu as the root of Cheongju and a center of history, where the city hall and the provincial office are located. It has places such as Sangdangsanseong Fortress (Sangdang Mountain Fortress), Cheongjueupseong (the Cheongju town walls), Yongdusaji Cheokdanggan (the iron flagpole of Yongdu Temple site), and Cheongju Hyanggyo (Cheongju local Confucian school). Mt. Uamsan, Daecheong Dam, the Munui Cultural Heritage Complex, and Cheongnamdae (the former presidential villa) are also in this district.

paras: Seowon-gu is a district that was newly created when Cheongju-si and Cheongwon-gun were joined in July 2014. The district names were chosen by public contest when the districts were divided. On May 30, 2013, the names Sangdang-gu, Seowon-gu, Heungdeok-gu, and Cheongwon-gu were decided. At first, Seowon-gu was made up of Nami-myeon and Hyeondo-myeon from Cheongwon-gun, and 9 dong from Cheongju-si.

The district office describes Seowon-gu as a district where city and countryside exist together, and as a center of education. It has universities such as Chungbuk National University, Cheongju National University of Education, and Seowon University, as well as a court and a prosecutors' office. It is also a center of culture and sports, with the Cheongju Arts Center, a main stadium, and a baseball stadium.

paras: Heungdeok-gu began as the Western Branch Office in July 1989. The Heungdeok-gu Office opened on January 1, 1995. When Cheongju-si and Cheongwon-gun were joined on July 1, 2014, it became Heungdeok-gu of the unified Cheongju-si. On July 1, 2021, the district office building moved to Sain-ri, Gangnae-myeon.

The district office describes Heungdeok-gu as a center of transport and logistics, where roads lead in every direction. It has Osong Station (a KTX high-speed train station) and the express and intercity bus terminals. There are also workplaces such as the Osong Bio-Science Complex and the Cheongju Industrial Complex. The district office also counts Heungdeoksaji (the site of Heungdeoksa Temple), Jikji (the book printed with movable metal type), the Baekje relics of Sinbong-dong, and the place where the Soro-ri rice grains were found as part of its history and culture.

paras: Cheongwon-gu was created when the Cheongwon-gu Office opened on July 1, 2014, as Cheongju-si and Cheongwon-gun were joined into one. At first it started with 2 eup (towns), 1 myeon (rural town), and 5 dong (neighborhoods). Cheongju and Cheongwon were split in two on June 1, 1946, and were joined again after 68 years.

The district office describes Cheongwon-gu as a place with good transport and a deep history and culture. It has Cheongju International Airport. The office points to Chojeong Yaksu (Chojeong mineral spring), Jeongbuk-dong Earthen Fortress, the site of Son Byeong-hui's former home, and Unbo's House (the home of the painter Unbo). It also has the Ochang Science and Industrial Complex, and farmland where people grow rice and garden crops.

paras: The Namhangang River (South Han River) flows through Chungju, and there is a wide area of limestone. Many cave sites where Paleolithic people lived remain there. In the Samhan period it belonged to Mahan, and around 350 it became Baekje land. In the middle of the 5th century, Goguryeo took the area and called it Gugwonseong, and it set up the Chungju Goguryeo Stele. King Jinheung of Silla set up Gugwon Sogyeong (Gugwon secondary capital) in 557, and the next year he made it the most important city after Gyeongju.

After Silla unified the Three Kingdoms, it built Tappyeong-ri Seven-story Stone Pagoda (also called Jungangtap, the Central Pagoda). Wang Geon, who founded Goryeo, changed the name of this place, then called Jungwon, to Chungju, and that name has lasted until today. In 1956, Chungju-eup (Chungju town) became Chungju-si (Chungju city), and in 1995 Chungju-si and Jungwon-gun were merged.

paras: In the Silla period, Jecheon was called Naeje-gun. After Goryeo was founded, it became Jeju (堤州). In the 9th year of King Hyeonjong of Goryeo, it was divided into Jeju-gun and Cheongpung-hyeon. In the Joseon period, it was called Jecheon-hyeon and Cheongpung-gun.

It became an eup (town) in the 1940s and a city (si) in 1980. In 1995, the city and the county were joined, and it became today's Jecheon-si. It lies in the middle of three national parks: Woraksan, Sobaeksan, and Chiaksan. It has Uirimji Pond, Baktaljae Pass, and Cheongpungho Lake. It is at the center of the inland middle region, where Chungcheongbuk-do, Gangwon-do, and Gyeongsangbuk-do meet. It is also a transport center where the Jungang Line, Taebaek Line, and Chungbuk Line railways meet. Festivals are held there too, such as the Cheongpungho Cherry Blossom Festival and the Jecheon International Music and Film Festival.

sources.t: Jecheon City Hall, General facts

paras: In the Samhan period, Boeun was Mahan land. In the Three Kingdoms period, it was a place where Baekje and Silla fought over the border. In 470, Silla built Samnyeonsanseong Fortress and used it as a base for moving north. In 502, this place was called Samnyeonsan-gun. In 757 it was changed to Samnyeon-gun, and after Goryeo unified the country, it was called Boryeong.

In 553, King Jinheung of Silla built Beopjusa Temple on Mt. Songnisan. In 1416, in the Joseon period, the name was changed to "Boeun (報恩)," and a hyeongam (a county magistrate) was posted there. It became Boeun-gun in 1895. In 1914, Hoein-gun was merged into it and it was organized into ten myeon (rural towns). In 1973, Boeun-myeon became Boeun-eup (Boeun town).

paras: In the Three Kingdoms period, Okcheon was called Gosisan-gun. In the time of King Gyeongdeok of Silla, the name was changed to Gwanseong, and in 1313, in the time of King Chungseon of Goryeo, it was raised to Okju. In 1413, in the time of King Taejong of Joseon, the name was changed to "Okcheon (沃川)," and it was moved from Gyeongsang-do to Chungcheong-do.

At Daecheon-ri, house sites from the Neolithic period, dated between 3500 and 3000 BC, were dug up. They are evidence that people settled there and farmed. On the floors of the house sites, things such as rice grains, barley, wheat, millet, and acorns were found, so we can learn what people ate at that time. At Anteo in Seoktan-ri there is a Bronze Age dolmen (a prehistoric stone tomb), and in Okcheon the Geumgang River winds around the rocks as it flows.

paras: In early Silla, Yeongdong was called Gildong. In the time of King Gyeongdeok of Unified Silla, the name was changed to "Yeongdong." According to the Yeongdong County Office, the name comes from the place in Yeongdong-eup where two streams meet. It explains that when "二水" (meaning two streams) is written as one character, it becomes "永."

In 1413 it was moved from Gyeongsang-do to Chungcheong-do. It became Yeongdong-gun in 1895, and in 1940 Yeongdong-myeon was raised to Yeongdong-eup. It is at the very south of Chungcheongbuk-do. It is where the Sobaek Mountains and the Noryeong Mountains split, so it is surrounded by mountains. Grapes, persimmons, walnuts, apples, and pears are the main farm products. It tends to be the warmest and sunniest place in Chungcheongbuk-do.

paras: In the Samhan period, Jeungpyeong belonged to Mahan. In the 5th century it was Goguryeo land, and after the 6th century it became Silla land. In 1914, several villages in the Geunseo-myeon area of Cheongan-gun were joined to make Jeungpyeong-ri. The name was made by taking the character "jeung" from Jeungcheon and the character "pyeong" from Jangpyeong. That year, Cheongan-gun was merged into Goesan-gun, and Jeungpyeong-myeon was created.

Jeungpyeong-myeon became Jeungpyeong-eup (Jeungpyeong town) in 1949, and in 1990 the Chungcheongbuk-do Jeungpyeong Branch Office was set up. Jeungpyeong-gun opened on August 30, 2003. Jeungpyeong is in the very middle of Chungcheongbuk-do. In the north, Mt. Dutasan, 598 m high, stretches long from east to west, and there are several mountains within 300 m in height on all sides.

paras: In the Goguryeo period, Jincheon was called Geummuno-gun (also said to be Manno-gun), and in the Silla period it was changed to Heugyang-gun. In early Goryeo it was called Jinju. In the 13th year of King Taejong of Joseon (1413), the name was changed to "Jincheon (鎭川)," and a hyeongam (a county magistrate) was posted there. In 1895 it became Jincheon-gun, with a gunsu (a county head) in place of the magistrate, and in 2019 Deoksan-myeon became Deoksan-eup.

The Charyeong Mountains pass through Jincheon, so there are many mountains. The Mihocheon Stream starts in Gwanghyewon-myeon and Baekgok-myeon and flows to the wide plain in the south. This plain is a granary region where grain grows well. It is an inland city that the Jungbu Expressway passes through. Farm products such as rice, watermelons, cucumbers, tomatoes, and melons are its main specialties.

paras: In 475, in the Goguryeo period, Goesan was called Ingeunnae-gun. In 757, in the Silla period, it was changed to Goeyang-gun, and in 940, in the Goryeo period, to Goeju-gun. In 1413, in the time of King Taejong of Joseon, it became Goesan-gun. In 1914, Yeonpung and Cheongan were merged with Goesan, and they became one Goesan-gun.

In the time of King Jinpyeong of Silla, General Chandeok did not surrender to the end, even when Baekje's army attacked him for a hundred days at Gajamseong Fortress. King Taejong Muyeol honored his spirit and had Gajamseong called "Goeyang (槐壤)," meaning land of the pagoda trees. In 1979, Goesan-myeon became Goesan-eup (Goesan town), and in 2003 Jeungpyeong-eup and Doan-myeon were split off to become Jeungpyeong-gun.

paras: Eumseong is a name that has been used for more than 1,200 years, since the Three Kingdoms period. In the Goguryeo period it was Inghol-hyeon (Inghol County), and in the 16th year of King Gyeongdeok of Silla (757), it was changed to Eumseong-hyeon (Eumseong County). "Inghol" means "wide fortress," and one theory says that when the name was changed into Chinese characters, the characters "eum (陰)" and "seong (城)" were probably chosen because they sound similar.

It became Eumseong-gun in 1895. In 1906, Geumwang-myeon, Saenggeuk-myeon, Sotan-myeon, Maengdong-myeon, Samseong-myeon, and Gamgok-myeon were added, and the area took its present form. Eumseong has long been a place with a lot of farming, so farm products such as red peppers, ginseng, peaches, and watermelons came from there. After the Jungbu Expressway opened in 1987, many companies moved in.

paras: Danyang is a place where people have lived since very long ago. In Geumgul Cave, which faces the Namhangang River (South Han River), finds from throughout the period from 700,000 to 3,000 years ago have been left behind. So it is a site that serves as a standard when studying prehistoric times. At Suyanggae, 50 places where people made stone tools were found. Traces of ancient people's lives also turned up at nearby Gunanggul Cave and the Sangsi rock shelter.

In the Three Kingdoms period, Danyang was Goguryeo land and then became Silla land. King Jinheung of Silla set up the Danyang Silla Red Stele to mark taking this place. The Goguryeo general Ondal died fighting below Adanseong (Ondal Fortress). In the early 1400s, in the time of King Taejong of Joseon, the name Danyang-gun was given, and in 1914 Yeongchun-gun was merged into Danyang.

paras: Cheonan-si is in the northeast of Chungcheongnam-do (South Chungcheong Province). To the east it meets Cheongju-si and Jincheon-gun in Chungcheongbuk-do. To the west is Asan-si, to the south are Gongju-si and Sejong-si, and to the north are Pyeongtaek-si and Anseong-si in Gyeonggi-do. The Taejosan (Mt. Taejo) ridge of the Charyeong Mountains runs north to south through the city and divides the east from the west. The north is open, low, hill-like flat land that stretches to the Pyeongtaek Plain.

In 1963, Cheonan-gun (county), Cheonan-eup (town), and Hwanseong-myeon (township) were joined to form Cheonan-si. At that time, Cheonan-gun was renamed Cheonwon-gun. In 1991, Cheonwon-gun became Cheonan-gun again. In 1995, Cheonan-si and Cheonan-gun were joined to make today's Cheonan-si. Cheonan City Hall says that the Gyeongbu Line runs north to south through the urban area, and the Janghang Line stretches to the southwest.

paras: Dongnam-gu is one of the two districts that make up Cheonan-si, and it was created in 2008 when Cheonan was divided into the two districts Dongnam-gu and Seobuk-gu. The district office is on Yetsicheong-gil. The district has towns and townships such as Mokcheon-eup, Byeongcheon-myeon, and Gwangdeok-myeon, and neighborhoods such as Sinbang-dong and Bongmyeong-dong. Mokcheon-eup was once the seat of Mokcheon-gun (county). In 1914, Mokcheon-gun was abolished and joined Cheonan-gun. Mokcheon became an eup (town) in 2002.

The Dongnam-gu Office describes the area as a place that produced many people who worked hard for the country, including the patriot Yu Gwan-sun. It lists sights such as the Independence Hall of Korea, Cheonan Samgeori (Cheonan Three-Way Crossroads), the Cheonan Museum, and Gwangdeoksan (Mt. Gwangdeok). Famous local foods are Gwangdeok walnuts, Byeongcheon cucumbers, Susin melons, and Pungse mushrooms.

paras: The Seobuk-gu Office is on Bongju-ro in Seonggeo-eup. The district has towns and townships such as Seonghwan-eup, Seonggeo-eup, Jiksan-eup, and Ipjang-myeon, and neighborhoods such as Seongjeong-dong, Buldang-dong, and Baekseok-dong. Seonghwan-eup took its name from the Seonghwan Dochalbang (a postal station office of the Joseon era) and became Seonghwan-myeon in 1914. It was raised to an eup (town) in 1973.

The Seobuk-gu Office says that this area is close to the Seoul metropolitan area. It also says that in 18 BC, King Onjo chose it as the first capital of Baekje (an ancient Korean kingdom) and built the foundation of the country here. Cheonan pears, Geobong grapes, and Heungtaryeong rice from Seonghwan are famous local products. The district office says that Samsung SDI and many other companies in the industrial complexes support the local economy.

paras: Gongju is where Ungjin, the old capital of Baekje (an ancient Korean kingdom), stood. King Munju of Baekje moved the capital to Ungjin in 475. Five kings ruled the country from here until King Seong moved the capital to Sabi in 538. In the Silla era, the place was called Ungcheonju in 686 and Ungju in 757. In 940, in the time of King Taejo of Goryeo, the name was changed to "Gongju."

In the Joseon era, Chungcheong Gamyeong (the provincial government office) was here, so Gongju was the center of the Chungcheong region. In 1895, Gongju-bu (prefecture) was created, and Gongju became the main town of Chungcheongnam-do (South Chungcheong Province). In 1932, the provincial office moved to Daejeon, and Gongju became a place with a county office. In 1986, Gongju-eup (town) became a city. On January 1, 1995, Gongju-si and Gongju-gun (county) were joined to form today's Gongju-si.

paras: Boryeong-gun (county) was reorganized in 1914 into a larger county by joining several old districts, including Nampo-gun and Ocheon-gun. The county office was moved to Daecheon-ri in Daecheon-myeon, and the county was divided into 10 townships. On January 1, 1963, Daecheon-myeon became Daecheon-eup (town). In 1983, some islands of Sapsido-ri in Ocheon-myeon were moved to Anmyeon-eup in Seosan-gun.

On January 1, 1986, Daecheon-eup became Daecheon-si (city) and was separated from Boryeong-gun. On March 27 of that year, the Seongju branch office became Seongju-myeon (township). On January 1, 1995, Daecheon-si and Boryeong-gun were joined and took the name Boryeong-si. On March 2 of that year, Ungcheon-myeon became an eup (town). The Boryeong Citizens' Charter describes the city as a place that holds Oseosan (Mt. Oseo), Seongjusan (Mt. Seongju), and a clean sea.

paras: Asan-si is at the far northwest end of Chungcheongnam-do (South Chungcheong Province). To the east it meets Cheonan-si, to the south Gongju-si, to the west Yesan-gun, and to the north Pyeongtaek-si in Gyeonggi-do. Asan City Hall says that in the Samhan era (the Three Han states), this area was the land of Yeomnoguk, a small state of Mahan. In the Baekje era, it belonged to Tangjeong-gun, Asul-hyeon, and Gulgik-hyeon (old districts).

In 1914, the three counties of Onyang, Asan, and Sinchang were joined to form Asan-gun (county). In 1986, Onyang-eup (town) was raised to Onyang-si (city) and separated. On January 1, 1995, Asan-gun and Onyang-si were joined to form today's Asan-si. Gwangdeoksan (Mt. Gwangdeok) is in the south and Yeonginsan (Mt. Yeongin) is in the north. The Gokgyocheon (Gokgyo Stream) meets the Sapgyocheon (Sapgyo Stream) and flows into Asan Bay. The Seohaean Expressway, the Gyeongbu Expressway, and the Janghang Line pass through the city.

paras: In the Samhan era (the Three Han states), Seosan belonged to Mahan. It is said that a small state called "Chirigukguk" once stood near today's Jigok-myeon. In 755, in the time of King Gyeongdeok of Unified Silla, it was Buseong-gun (county). In 894, Choe Chi-won is said to have come to govern the district. In 1284, in the Goryeo era, it was first called "Seosan."

Until the Joseon era, Seosan was raised to a gun (county) and lowered to a hyeon (a smaller district) several times. In 1914, Taean and Haemi were joined to it. In 1942, Seosan-myeon (township) became an eup (town). On January 1, 1989, Seosan-eup became a city, and the area was divided into Seosan-si, Seosan-gun, and Taean-gun. In January 1995, Seosan-si and Seosan-gun were joined.

sources.t: Seosan City Hall, History and origin of the name

paras: People have lived in Nonsan since prehistoric times. In the Samhan era (the Three Han states), Mahan was here, and in the Three Kingdoms era, Baekje was here. It is said that 5,000 soldiers led by General Gyebaek and 50,000 soldiers led by Silla General Kim Yu-sin fought Baekje's last battle on Hwangsanbeol (the Hwangsan Plain). In the Goryeo and Joseon eras, there were four districts: Yeonsan, Eunjin, Noseong, and Seokseong.

In 1912, the four districts became four counties. In 1914, the four counties were joined to form Nonsan-gun (county). It became a city on March 1, 1996. On September 19, 2003, Duma-myeon (township) was separated to become Gyeryong-si. The Nonsan City Hall website says that Nonsan lies in the lower belly of the Korean Peninsula, which is shaped like a tiger, the place that is the source of its strength.

sources.t: Nonsan City Hall, History

paras: Gyeryong-si is a new city that opened on September 19, 2003. In 1914, it was Duma-myeon (township) of Nonsan-gun (county). This Duma-myeon was separated from Nonsan and became Gyeryong-si. The law that created the city was announced on July 18 of that year, and the first city council opened on November 6.

In 1989, the Army Headquarters and the Air Force Headquarters moved to Gyeryongdae (the Gyeryong military base). In 1993, the Navy Headquarters moved there too. In 1990, in between, the Chungcheongnam-do Gyeryong branch office was set up. In 1991, the President ordered that "Gyeryong New Town" be designated as a special area. In its city vision, Gyeryong-si puts forward "completing the national defense capital." On its website, the city says it will make the "smallest but most prosperous city" in the world.

paras: Dangjin was Mahan land in the Samhan (Three Han) period. In the Baekje period, Hye-gun, a district in the Myeoncheon area, governed a wide region. In the reign of King Gyeongdeok of Unified Silla, Beolsuji-hyeon (a county) around today's Dangjin-eup was renamed Dangjin-hyeon. In 1413, in the reign of King Taejong of Joseon, a magistrate was posted there again, and it became Dangjin-hyeon of Chungcheong-do (Chungcheong Province).

It became Dangjin-gun in 1895. In 1914, Myeoncheon-gun and others were merged, and the county was reorganized into 10 myeon (townships). Dangjin-myeon became an eup (town) in 1963, Hapdeok-myeon in 1973, and Songak-myeon on January 1, 2010. Dangjin became a city on January 1, 2012. It is a wide plain in the north of Chungnam, and farming and the steel industry are said to be growing together there.

paras: In the Baekje period, Geumsan was called Jinnae-gun. In the reign of King Gyeongdeok of Unified Silla, it was renamed Jinye-gun. In 1305, it was raised to Geumju-gun. In 1413, in the reign of King Taejong of Joseon, Geumju-gun was renamed Geumsan-gun.

Today's Geumsan-gun was created on March 1, 1914, by combining the old Geumsan-gun with other counties. At that time it had 10 myeon (townships), including Geumsan-myeon, Geumseong-myeon, and Jewon-myeon. In 1940, Geumsan-myeon became Geumsan-eup (a town), making it 1 eup and 9 myeon. Geumsan belonged to Jeollabuk-do (North Jeolla Province) from 1896, and joined Chungcheongnam-do (South Chungcheong Province) on January 1, 1963.

sources.t: Geumsan County Office, History of Geumsan

paras: Buyeo was the last capital of Baekje. In 538, King Seong of Baekje moved the capital here from Ungjin (today's Gongju) and called it "Sabi." Six kings, from King Seong to King Uija, used this place as their capital. After Baekje fell to the Silla-Tang allied forces in 660, the name Buyeo-gun was given in the reign of King Gyeongdeok of Silla (742-765).

The Songguk-ri culture is said to have flourished in Buyeo about 2,500 years ago, in the Bronze Age. In 1413, in the Joseon period, it became independent as Buyeo-hyeon (a county). In 1914, Hongsan-hyeon, Imcheon-gun, and others were merged to form Buyeo-gun, made up of 16 myeon (townships). On January 1, 1960, Buyeo-myeon became an eup (town), so today it has 1 eup and 15 myeon.

sources.t: Buyeo County Office, History

paras: Seocheon-gun is in the southwest of Chungnam. Buyeo-gun is to the east, the West Sea (Yellow Sea) is to the west, and Boryeong-si is to the north. To the south, it faces Gunsan-si across the Geumgang River (Geum River). Seocheon County Office regards the start of government in this area as the founding of Arim-guk, a small state of Mahan in the Samhan (Three Han) period. It says Arim-guk was near Namsan (South Mountain) in today's Seocheon-eup. In 1413 (the 13th year of King Taejong of Joseon), Seorim-gun was renamed Seocheon-gun.

Seocheon has long been known for the fine ramie cloth of Hansan, and it is still known today as the home of ramie. Geonjisanseong Fortress in Hansan was an important place guarding the west of Baekje. After Baekje fell, the people who remained tried for three years to revive the country, centered on this area.

paras: Cheongyang-gun is in the middle of Chungnam. Gongju-si is to the east, Boryeong-si to the west, Buyeo-gun to the south, and Yesan-gun to the north. Cheongyang County Office says that in the Baekje period this area was divided into three hyeon (counties): Yeolgi-hyeon, Goryangburi-hyeon, and Sasiryang-hyeon. In the Silla period, they were renamed Yeolseong-hyeon, Cheongjeong-hyeon, and Sinryang-hyeon. In the Goryeo period, Cheongjeong-hyeon became Cheongyang-hyeon.

In 1895, Cheongyang-hyeon and Jeongsan-hyeon each became a gun (county). In 1914, the two were merged to form Cheongyang-gun. In 1942, Eupnae-myeon was renamed Cheongyang-myeon, and in 1979 Cheongyang-myeon was raised to Cheongyang-eup (a town). In the southeast of the county, mountain ridges stretching from Chilgapsan Mountain rise up. The Geumgang River (Geum River) flows through the southeast, and Jicheoncheon Stream and Inghwacheon Stream also flow south and join the Geumgang River.

paras: Hongseong-gun was formed by joining the old Hongju-gun and Gyeolseong-gun. Hongseong County Office says that in 1914, Hongju-gun, Gyeolseong-gun, and part of Boryeong-gun were merged to become Hongseong-gun. In 1941, Hongju-myeon became Hongseong-eup (a town), and in 2017, Hongbuk-myeon became Hongbuk-eup.

Hongseong-gun is in the central west of Chungnam. To the west, it faces Anmyeondo Island of Taean-gun across Cheonsuman Bay. Low hills spread around Bongsusan Mountain in the east, Baegwolsan Mountain in the west, Oseosan Mountain in the south, and Yongbongsan Mountain in the north, so the land is fairly flat. After Baekje fell, fighting to revive Baekje took place around Imjonseong Fortress on Bongsusan Mountain. Hongseong County Office describes the area itself as the birthplace of great, loyal figures such as Choe Yeong, Seong Sam-mun, Kim Jwa-jin, and Han Yong-un.

paras: The name Yesan was given in 919, the 2nd year of King Taejo of Goryeo. Yesan County Office says this place was originally Osan-hyeon of Baekje. In the reign of King Gyeongdeok of Silla it was renamed Gosan, and in the Goryeo period it became Yesan. The year 2019 marked 1,100 years since the name Yesan was first used.

Yesan-gun is in the northwest of Chungnam. Asan-si and Gongju-si are to the east, Cheongyang-gun is to the south, Hongseong-gun and Seosan-si are to the west, and Dangjin-si and Asan-si are to the north. In 1914, the three counties of Yesan, Daeheung, and Deoksan were merged to form Yesan-gun. In 1917, Imseong-myeon was renamed Yesan-myeon, and in 1940 Yesan-myeon was raised to an eup (town). From Yesan-eup, roads spread out in four directions, toward Asan, Dangjin, Hongseong, and Gongju.

paras: The name Taean came about in 1298, the 24th year of King Chungnyeol of Goryeo, when Sotae-hyeon was renamed Taean and raised to a gun (county). Taean County Office explains that "Taean" is a short form of "gukpyeong minan," meaning the country is at peace and the people are safe. During the Japanese colonial period, in 1914, it was merged into Seosan-gun. It became a county again on January 1, 1989.

Taean-gun is a peninsula surrounded by sea on three sides, all except the east. It has the only coastal national park in Korea, as well as the pine forests and beaches of Anmyeondo Island, and many islands with legends. Neolithic shell mounds were found in Gonam-myeon and Nam-myeon, so people are thought to have lived here from about 4,500 to 5,000 years ago.

paras: Pohang was the site of Toehwa-hyeon, Jida-hyeon, Geunoji-hyeon and Haea-hyeon (counties) in the Silla period. In the Goryeo period they became Heunghae-gun, Janggi-hyeon, Yeongil-hyeon and Cheongha-hyeon. Under the 13-province system of 1896, they became four counties: Heunghae, Cheongha, Yeongil and Janggi. In 1914 these four counties were merged into Yeongil-gun.

In 1931 Pohang-myeon (township) became Pohang-eup (town), and in 1949 Pohang-eup was raised to Pohang-si (city). In 1995 the new, integrated Pohang-si was launched, and in 2010 Daebo-myeon was renamed Homigot-myeon. In 1942 Changju-myeon became Guryongpo-eup. Seokbyeong-ri in Guryongpo-eup is described as the easternmost point of the Korean Peninsula.

paras: On January 1, 1995, the new Pohang-si, which combined city and countryside, started, and district offices were set up at that time. Nam-gu has eups (towns) such as Guryongpo-eup, Yeongil-eup and Ocheon-eup, and dongs (neighborhoods) such as Sangdae-dong and Songdo-dong.

Nam-gu is home to POSCO, a world-class steel company that led the way in the great growth of the nation's industry. It also has the Homigot Sunrise Plaza, famous for its beautiful sunrises, and Cheolgilsup (Railroad Forest), called the green heart of the Greenway Project. The district office also introduces Oeosa Temple on Mount Unje (Unjesan), which keeps the stories of the Buddhist masters Wonhyo and Jajang, as well as the Yeonorang and Seonyeo Theme Park and the Guryongpo Japanese House Street.

paras: Buk-gu was created on January 1, 1995, when the new Pohang-si, combining city and countryside, was launched and a district office was set up. It has myeons (townships) such as Songna-myeon and Gigye-myeon, and dongs (neighborhoods) such as Duho-dong and Jukdo-dong.

Buk-gu has Hwanho Park, and inside it are the Space Walk and the city art museum. Mount Naeyeon (Naeyeonsan), where the thousand-year-old temple Bogyeongsa stands, has twelve waterfalls. Jukdo Market is described as one of the five major traditional markets in Korea. KTX Pohang Station, the East Coast Expressway and Yeongilman Port are the axes of Pohang's tourism, culture and industry, and the Yeongilman Industrial Complex is also a place the district office introduces.

paras: Gyeongju was the capital of Silla for 992 years. Silla began when the village heads of six clans on the Gyeongju Plain made Bak Hyeokgeose their king. In 935, the 18th year of King Taejo of Goryeo, the place was called Gyeongju, and in 1413, in the Joseon period, it became Gyeongju-bu (a prefecture).

Under King Beopheung, Silla officially recognized Buddhism, and Buddhist culture began to shine. In 676 Silla achieved the unification of the Three Kingdoms. In Gyeongju, Gyeongju-myeon (township) was raised to a eup (town) in 1931, and Gyeongju-eup was raised to a si (city) in 1955. On January 1, 1995, the integrated Gyeongju-si was launched, and in 2021 Yangbuk-myeon was renamed Munmudaewang-myeon.

paras: Gimcheon was the site of Gammun-guk (also called Gamno-guk) and Jujoma-guk in the Samhan period. In 1914 the three counties of Gimsan, Jirye and Gaeryeong were combined with Singok-myeon of Seongju, and the new county was called Gimcheon-gun. In 1949 Gimcheon-eup was raised to Gimcheon-bu and then became Gimcheon-si, and Gimcheon-gun was renamed Geumneung-gun.

In 1995 Gimcheon-si and Geumneung-gun were merged into one, and in the same year Apo-myeon was raised to Apo-eup. In 2014 Yulgok-dong was newly created. The Gimcheon City website describes Gimcheon as a place with fine mountains and clean water, and says that in the Joseon period it was once one of the five biggest markets in the country.

sources.t: Gimcheon City Hall, About Gimcheon · Timeline (last revised August 25, 2025)

paras: The name Andong was given in 930, the 13th year of King Taejo of Goryeo. When Wang Geon and Gyeon Hwon fought at Byeongsan, the people of this town helped Wang Geon. For this service, the town was raised to a bu (prefecture) and its name was changed to Andong. In 1895 a gwancharbu (a regional government office) was set up in Andong to govern 17 counties in the northeast of Gyeongsang-do (Gyeongsang Province), and in 1896 it was changed to Andong-gun.

In 1963 Andong-eup was raised to a city and became Andong-si, and in 1974 Wolgok-myeon disappeared when Andong Dam was built. In 1995 Andong-si and Andong-gun were merged. The Andong City website says that Andong Hahoe Village was listed as a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2010, and that the Confucian Printing Woodblocks (Yugyo Chaekpan) were listed in the Memory of the World Register in 2015.

paras: The land of today's Gumi became Seonsan-gun in 1413, in the Joseon period. In 1978 Gumi-eup of Seonsan-gun and Indong-myeon of Chilgok-gun were combined and raised to Gumi-si. In 1995 Gumi-si and Seonsan-gun were merged to form today's Gumi-si.

The Gumi City website says that the Nakdong River (Nakdonggang) flows through the middle of the city, and that there are mountains such as Geumosan (976 m above sea level), Cheonsaengsan and Naengsan. It also says that Buddhism first came to the Korean Peninsula here in the Silla period, and that Dorisa Temple, said to be the first temple in Haedong (Korea), is here. In the Joseon period, it is said, this was a place where Neo-Confucianism flourished, and scholars such as Yaeun Gil Jae and Jeompiljae Kim Jong-jik came from here.

paras: Yeongju was once the site of Naegi-gun and Geupbalsan-gun of Goguryeo, but King Pasa of Silla took it, and around AD 100 it became Silla land. In 1259, in the Goryeo period, it got the name 'Yeongju'. In the Joseon period, the name 'Punggi' was made from the names of two towns, Eunpung and Gicheon, and in 1914 Yeongcheon-gun, Punggi-gun and Sunheung-gun were merged to form Yeongju-gun.

In 1980 Yeongju-eup became Yeongju-si, and in 1995 Yeongju-si and Yeongpung-gun were merged into one. Yeongju lies at the foot of Sobaeksan Mountain, and the Namwoncheon and Jukgyecheon streams join to form Seocheon, which then flows into the Nakdong River. The mountain area in the north drains water well, and it is described as a good place for growing ginseng and apples.

paras: In Yeongcheon, at the place where the Geumhogang River begins, there are remains where prehistoric people lived. In the Samhan period there was a small state called Golbulsoguk, and in 757, in the Silla period, it was renamed Imgo-gun. In 1413, under King Taejong of Joseon, Yeongju (永州) was renamed Yeongcheon-gun (永川郡), and in 1914 Sinnyeong-gun was merged into Yeongcheon-gun.

In 1981 Yeongcheon-eup became Yeongcheon-si, and in 1995 Yeongcheon-si and Yeongcheon-gun were merged to form today's Yeongcheon-si. It is a transport hub, crossed by the Jungang Line and Daegu Line railways and the Gyeongbu Expressway. Yeongcheon City introduces wine and grapes, a herbal medicine market, and the stories of Jeong Mong-ju and General Choe Mu-seon as features of Yeongcheon.

paras: Sangju is a place where, according to the Samguk Sagi and the Samguk Yusa (old history books), the country of Sabeol-guk once stood. Sabeol-guk is thought to have been merged into Silla in AD 249, and in 525, under King Beopheung, Silla set up Sabeol-ju. In 757, under King Gyeongdeok, Sabeol-ju was renamed Sangju, the name it has today.

The name Gyeongsang-do (Gyeongsang Province) is also linked to Sangju. It is said that in 1314, the first year of King Chungsuk of Goryeo, the province was renamed Gyeongsang-do, taking the first letters of Gyeongju and Sangju. In 1931 Sangju-myeon was raised to a eup, and in 1986 Sangju-eup was raised to a si. In 1995 the city and the county were merged, and Sangju-si was formed, with city and countryside together.

sources.t: Sangju City Hall, History of Sangju

paras: Mungyeong lies inland, at the far northwest of Gyeongsangbuk-do (North Gyeongsang Province). To the east it borders Yecheon-gun, to the south Sangju-si, and to the west Goesan-gun of Chungcheongbuk-do. To the north it borders Jecheon-si, Chungju-si and Danyang-gun of Chungcheongbuk-do. In 1390, the 2nd year of King Gongyang of Goryeo, the post of gammu (a local official) was placed in Mungyeong-gun.

In 1895 Mungyeong-gun was abolished and divided among neighboring counties, but in 1896 it returned as Mungyeong-gun. In 1914 Seo-myeon of Yonggung-gun and part of Dong-myeon of Hamchang-eup were added, and the shape of today's city was formed. In 1986 Jeomchon-eup became Jeomchon-si, and on January 1, 1995, Jeomchon-si and Mungyeong-gun were merged to form Mungyeong-si.

paras: Long ago, in the Samhan period, Gyeongsan was the land of Amnyang-soguk, also called Apdok-guk, a small state that belonged to Byeonjin. It was merged into Silla in AD 102, and in 642 Silla set up Amnyang-ju here and made Kim Yu-sin its head. In 1310, the 2nd year of King Chungseon of Goryeo, the name Jangsan was changed to Gyeongsan.

In 1989 Gyeongsan-eup became a city, and in 1995 Gyeongsan-si and Gyeongsan-gun were merged. Palgongsan Mountain to the north is a high mountain, 1,193 m above sea level. It was known in the Silla period as Jungak and Buak, and it has Silla-period temples such as Wonhyosa and Bulgulsa. Hwanseongsan Mountain on the Hayang side is said to have got its name because the shape of the mountain looks like rings hooked together and pulling at each other.

paras: Uiseong is where a country called Jomunguk once stood long ago. The only record of Jomunguk in the Samguk Sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms) is one line saying that Silla "punished" it in 185. In 757, Jomun-gun became Munso-gun and belonged to Sangju.

Around Jomunguk's capital, in Geumseong-myeon and Bongyang-myeon, there are dolmens. In Geumseong-myeon, ancient tombs are scattered in several places. In 1960, diggers at the Tapri-ri tombs found a gilt-bronze crown and many clay pots. The gilt-bronze crown looks like a crown of the Jomunguk kings. In 1895, Uiseong became a county, and in 1940, Uiseong-myeon became Uiseong-eup (a town).

paras: Cheongsong was called Cheonggi-hyeon under Goguryeo and Jeokseon under Silla. In the Goryeo period, it went through the names Buyi and Unbong, and then became Cheongbu under King Seongjong. In the Joseon period, it became Cheongsong-gun under King Sejong. In 1459, under King Sejo, it was raised to Cheongsong-dohobu (protectorate), and in 1895 it became Cheongsong-gun again.

In the east of Cheongsong-gun, rugged mountains such as the Taebaek Mountains and Juwangsan Mountain continue on. Juwanggyegok Valley on Juwangsan Mountain and Jusanji Pond are Scenic Sites designated by the nation, and Bogwangjeon Hall of Daejeonsa Temple is a Treasure. In 1914, part of Jinbo-gun was joined to the county. In 1979, Cheongsong-myeon became Cheongsong-eup (a town), and in 2019, Budong-myeon was renamed Juwangsan-myeon.
